source.description: SYNTHETIC WORKED EXAMPLE -- not a real chip's register map. Fabricated deliberately and labeled as such so dv_harness/sys_regmap.py and dv_harness/init_seq.py have something real to be exercised against without any project's confidential programming guide entering this repo. A real project replaces this file wholesale with content transcribed from its own chip-level programming guide. Per CLAUDE.md's Evidence Truth Rule, nothing here is evidence about any real DUT.

fields.name: usb0_clk_en
fields.description: Gates usb0's functional clock. With this at 0 the usb0 clock never toggles, which a Gate-2 zero-time connectivity check would otherwise report as a connectivity failure.

fields.name: revision_id
fields.description: Read-only revision field sharing this register; transcribed for fidelity, explicitly not a mode bit.

fields.name: usb0_rst_release
fields.description: Releases usb0 from reset. Must be written AFTER usb0_clk_en per the init sequence -- releasing reset on an unclocked block leaves it in an undefined state.

fields.name: usb0_pad_sel
fields.description: Selects usb0 onto the shared pads. At its 0x0 reset value the pads are owned by a different function and usb0 sees no external activity at all.

fields.name: global_pad_ie
fields.description: Global pad input enable. Deliberately carries required_value null and an EMPTY governs_interfaces list -- this exercises the two honesty paths in sys_regmap.py: an unscoped mode bit applies to EVERY interface, and an undocumented required value is reported as unverifiable rather than guessed.
